stories.headline: Sources: Packers to put WR Jayden Reed on IR due to neck injury
stories.summary: The Packers are placing wide receiver Jayden Reed on injured reserve due to the neck injury he suffered in Week 2 against the Jets, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter.
stories.body:
The Green Bay Packers are placing wide receiver Jayden Reed on injured reserve due to the neck injury he suffered in Week 2 against the New York Jets, sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter.

Reed, 26, is out indefinitely, if not for the season, as he continues his recovery.

Apparently reacting to the news, he posted to Instagram on Wednesday: "God will use the unusual to do the unexpected... 11 out."

Reed, who signed a three-year, $50.25 million contract extension in April, has four receptions for 24 yards in two games this season.

A second-round pick of the Packers in 2023, he has 142 catches for 1,881 yards and 18 total touchdowns in his career.

stories.headline: 2026 MLB wild-card series Day 2: Live updates, lineups, analysis
stories.summary: Which teams will sweep and which will force a Game 3? We've got it all covered for you.
stories.body:
Who is ready for some more postseason baseball?

After an exciting opening to the MLB playoffs, it's time for four more games Wednesday. Will the Atlanta Braves finish off the the Philadelphia Phillies after a dramatic comeback win in Game 1? Will the New York Yankees knock out the rival Boston Red Sox? Will the Chicago White Sox sweep the Houston Astros? And can the Chicago Cubs turn on their offense after they were shut out against the San Diego Padres?

We've got you covered with pregame lineups, sights and sounds from the ballparks and postgame takeaways as each Day 2 matchup ends.

Philadelphia Phillies vs. Atlanta Braves

Atlanta leads 1-0

2 p.m. ET

Game 2 starters: Cristopher Sanchez vs. Tyler Mahle

What the Phillies need to do to force Game 3: Philadelphia has its ace going in Game 2 against Atlanta's Mahle. That's a big edge for the Phillies on the mound, and it's easy to imagine Sanchez dealing late into the game -- he has averaged more than six innings per start this season -- as they cruise to a win to even the series. They also have stars who can hit in big spots -- when J.T. Realmuto hit a triple in the top of the seventh of Game 1 to give the Phillies the lead, it seemed as if this series was headed in a different direction. That is, until Austin Riley's dramatic three-run homer in the bottom of the eighth. But Philly has still shown it has what it takes to win. -- Kiley McDaniel

What the Astros need to do to force Game 3: They need to play a more crisp game -- better at-bats and better command from their pitchers. They have the on-paper pitching edge with Hunter Brown starting and key relievers Josh Hader and Bryan Abreu more or less fresh after zipping through an inning each in Game 1. By contrast, White Sox relief ace Grant Taylor logged 54 pitches. Still, more than anything, Houston needs to generate more energy than it did Tuesday. Beyond the obvious, though, the Red Sox need Sonny Gray to be who he was in his last wild-card round start in 2023, when he threw five scoreless innings for Minnesota. A lineup that was dead last in runs scored during September -- 71 in 24 games -- needs to find itself fast. Red Sox players exuded calm following their Game 1 loss, leaning on the previous holes this season that they've dug and climbed out of. stories.headline: Which Premier League players got injured in the international break?
stories.summary: All the latest news and updates on Premier League stars injuries during the first international break of the 2026-2027 club season
stories.body:
Premier League teams will be watching and hoping their star players remain healthy throughout the international break.

However, some have already sustained injuries while playing for their countries. Premier League matches resume on Oct. 10.

ESPN will be tracking the latest injuries and updates for your club's players:

Kai Havertz (Arsenal)

Arsenal's Kai Havertz was forced off in the 30th minute of the game between Netherlands and Germany on September 24th with what was described as a muscle injury.

"Both are currently undergoing an MRI," Jurgen Klopp said on RTL about Havertz and Jamal Musiala. "I hope we get the diagnosis [on Thursday] evening. But of course, this isn't great. I hope it's nothing serious. The lads are probably out for us. But hopefully, they'll be back in action relatively quickly."

On September 25 the German Football Association confirmed the attacker would be leaving Klopp's camp and return to Arsenal after suffering what they describe as a 'muscle strain.'

Brian Brobbey (Sunderland)

The powerful Sunderland attacker was also injured in the same game after picking up what looked like a hamstring injury while running for the ball. He immediately went down and signalled to the sideline.

He left the field of his own accord but did have a heavy limp as he walked down the tunnel.

Netherlands boss Xavi Hernandez said after the game: "Brian is indeed injured."

Brobbey was replaced by Joshua Zirkzee in the Dutch squad.

Zion Suzuki (Aston Villa)

The goalkeeper linked up with the Japan squad but according to reports missed the main group training session on September 22nd, according to local reports. Instead he was put on an individual session for a rib injury.

Suzuki was subsequently left out of Japan's matchday squad entirely for Thursday's 3-1 victory over Uruguay.

Dan Ballard (Sunderland)

The Sunderland defender suffered a reported hamstring injury during Northern Ireland's 1-0 victory over Georgia in the UEFA Nations League.

With the score still 0-0 as the match moved into stoppage time, Ballard chased back as Georgia counter-attacked and pulled up clutching the back of his thigh, unable to finish the match in Tbilisi.

Speaking immediately after Friday's match, manager Michael O'Neill said it was too soon to know the extent of his latest injury but will definitely miss the next three Northern Ireland games.

"We'll scan him tomorrow (Saturday), but he's certainly not going to be available for the next three games."

Alexander Isak (Liverpool)

Alexander Isak is returning to Liverpool after sustaining a "minor injury" on international duty.

The striker scored and played the full 90 minutes in Sweden's 2-1 victory over Romania in the Nations League on Friday.

But Isak, who has made a strong start to the season for Liverpool, will not feature in matches against Poland, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Romania over the remainder of the extended international break.

Bruno Fernandes (Manchester United)

The Manchester United midfielder was left out of Portugal's squad for Sunday's game against Norway.

"He played with an injury he brought from Manchester United," Portugal boss Jorge Jesus said. "He really wanted to play against Wales."

Patrick Dorgu (Manchester United)

The news for Manchester United fans who saw Fernandes absent worsened on Sunday when Dorgu was injured.

The left wing-back limped out of Denmark's match against Wales after 30 minutes.

Denmark head coach Brian Riemer told broadcaster TV2 after the game: "He has an injury and has to go home."

Cody Gakpo (Liverpool)

Liverpool forward Gakpo lasted only 17 minutes of the Netherlands' match against Serbia on Sunday. It means Liverpool are sweating over the fitness of Isak and Gakpo.

He looked in pain as he held the lower part of his right leg.

"It's his ankle, that's all I know," Netherlands boss Xavi Hernández said. "Tomorrow we will know, but hopefully it's not too important."

Noussair Mazraoui (Manchester United)

The United full-back was forced out of Morocco's Africa Cup of Nations qualifier against Lesotho after 69 minutes. He was holding his back while on the floor after a challenge.

Nico O'Reilly (Manchester City)

O'Reilly missed England's win against Czechia on Tuesday night after also missing training on Monday. Liverpool winger Rio Ngumoha was called into the matchday squad.

Jan Paul van Hecke (Tottenham Hotspur)

The Tottenham defender Jan Paul van Hecke picked up a foot injury in the Netherlands' clash with Serbia and withdrew from the Netherlands' squad during a training session.

No replacement will be called up for van Hecke. He is now returning to Spurs.

International breaks this season

1. Sept. 21-Oct. 6 (between Premier League gameweeks 5 and 6)

2. Nov. 9-Nov. 17 (between Premier League gameweeks 10 and 11)

3. March 22-March 30 (between Premier League gameweeks 30 and 31)

stories.headline: Avalanche signing coach Jared Bednar to four-year extension
stories.summary: After he was set to coach on the final season of his contract, the Avalanche's Jared Bednar is getting a four-year extension.
stories.body:
The Colorado Avalanche have agreed to terms on a four-year contract extension with coach Jared Bednar, the team announced Wednesday.

The move alleviates any concern about Bednar's future in Colorado. The winningest coach in franchise history had been set to be behind the bench for the 2026-27 season on the final year of his contract before the extension.

General manager Joe Sakic said in June that Bednar and his staff would return, but there was some uncertainty after the Presidents' Trophy-winning Avalanche were stunned in a Western Conference finals sweep by the Vegas Golden Knights.

"Jared has done an outstanding job over the last decade, and there's no doubt in my mind he's the best coach for this group," Sakic said in a statement announcing the new deal. "He commands the room and has complete confidence of the players. We're excited to continue to have him in charge, and we believe that his presence maximizes the team's potential while this core group is intact."

Bednar, who said leading into training camp that they were in discussions to get a deal completed, is now signed through the 2030-31 season.

Colorado has reached the playoffs in eight of Bednar's nine seasons as coach, winning the Stanley Cup in 2021-22 behind a nucleus that included Cale Makar, Nathan MacKinnon and captain Gabriel Landeskog. He has a 445-262-75 record during his tenure.

The Avalanche, who set a franchise record with 121 points in 2025-26, open their regular season Wednesday by hosting the Los Angeles Kings.

Bednar is the second-longest tenured coach in the NHL behind only the Tampa Bay Lightning's Jon Cooper, who was hired in 2013.

"I'm extremely happy and grateful to continue leading this group," Bednar said in a statement. "My family and I have loved being a part of this organization from the beginning, and I can't thank the Kroenke family and Joe Sakic enough for their support. I look forward to working hard each day this season and beyond to accomplish our goal of winning another Stanley Cup."

Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

stories.headline: Philadelphia Union, USMNT's Cavan Sullivan becomes youngest MLS Player of the Month
stories.summary: Philadelphia Union and USMNT midfielder Cavan Sullivan became the youngest player in MLS history to be named Player of the Month on Wednesday when he was awarded the honors for September.
stories.body:
Philadelphia Union and United States men's national team midfielder Cavan Sullivan became the youngest player in MLS history to be named Player of the Month on Wednesday when he was awarded the honors for September.

At 16, Cavan Sullivan became the youngest player to start a game for the United States since Freddy Adu in 2006 when he was picked in Mauricio Pochettino's XI for Saturday's 4-1 friendly win vs. Peru.

He was one of 11 players -- including seven other teenagers -- to make their first appearances for the U.S. in that game against Peru.

Sullivan, who turned 17 on Sept. 28, came on as a substitute on Tuesday in the USMNT's 4-2 friendly win over Chile.

Sullivan has seven goals and 12 assists in 26 games for the Union, who have surged up to sixth place in the Eastern Conference in recent weeks. He has played 1,675 league minutes in MLS.

His 19 goal contributions are tied with Alphonso Davies (2018) for the second-most by a teenager in an MLS season, trailing only Diego Fagundez (20 in 2013).

Since returning from the World Cup break, the Union have recorded 32 points during a 12-game unbeaten streak, which is tied for the most points by a club in a 12-game span in MLS history. Sullivan has started all 11 of those games, logging a goal contribution in eight of them.

Sullivan and the Union will return after the FIFA international break on Oc. 10 to host Real Salt Lake at Subaru Park (7:30 p.m. ET).

NBA training camps have officially begun!

Monday marked the arrival of media day for most of the league's 30 teams, with on-court practice beginning Tuesday -- exactly three weeks before the New York Knicks will raise their 2026 NBA championship banner.

We have you covered as you dig into the 2026-27 season, with roster breakdowns for all 30 teams, top storylines, decisions and lingering issues to watch over the next few weeks.

Atlanta Hawks

What to watch during training camp: the frontcourt

Despite the franchise's run to the Eastern Conference's No. 6 seed, Atlanta's lack of frontcourt size was a major weakness. The Hawks' defense ranked 18th in blocks and 29th in both second-chance and point paints allowed during the regular season. And in the playoffs, Atlanta trailed only the Denver Nuggets in second chance points allowed per game. Selecting forward Zuby Ejiofor at No. 23 in June's draft and re-signing center Jock Landale, who missed the Hawks' first-round defeat because of a right ankle sprain, will help. Mouhamed Gueye (fractured foot; might miss the start of 2026-27) and Henri Veesaar (torn right ACL; expected to miss the season).

What to watch during training camp: the offense

Over the past four regular seasons, Boston has won 73% of its games while also ranking in the top four leaguewide in 3-point attempts. But the Celtics' first-round loss to the Philadelphia 76ers revealed cracks in the NBA's second-ranked offense.

"The biggest thing is can we generate looks at the rim?" Celtics president of basketball operations Brad Stevens said. "Everybody wants to do that, and every one of us would prefer a dunk over a 3. Every single one of us. Those are hard to get, and we struggle to generate them."

With Jaylen Brown replaced by Paul George and Mitchell Robinson signed to provide frontcourt help, will the Celtics adjust their philosophy? Per Cleaning the Glass, George ranked in the 90th percentile among wings in midrange attempts. For his part, George also shot better than 39% on 3s for the ninth time in his career last season.

What to watch during training camp: former first-rounders, playmaking and rim protection

The Nets drafted an NBA-record five first-round picks in 2025. For the roster to grow, there needs to be positive development in their sophomore season. Of the five former first-rounders, only Egor Demin averaged at least 25 minutes.

Brooklyn added 2026 No. 6 pick Mikel Brown Jr. and traded for Julius Randle, but did those moves give the Nets enough playmaking to the roster? In his freshman season at Louisville, Brown averaged 4.7 assists per game. And in the lineups where Minnesota did not play with a point guard, Randle averaged 5.0 assists per game.

The Nets also lack rim protection after starting center Nic Claxton was traded to Chicago as part of the Randle deal. Day'Ron Sharpe and Moritz Wagner, the only centers on Brooklyn's roster, averaged a combined 1.0 block per 36 minutes last season. The Nets allowed the seventh most points in the paint in 2025-26.

What to watch during training camp: the backcourt and Brandon Miller

Coby White will assume the starting role after Charlotte traded former franchise guard LaMelo Ball to the Minnesota Timberwolves.

It should be a relatively smooth transition. White came off the bench in the 21 games after he was acquired from Chicago in February; but before the deal, he had started 97% of the games he played from 2023-24. And in the contests White played without Ball, the Hornets were plus-18.7 points per 100 possessions.

The Ball trade also was a bet on the development of Miller, who is currently rookie-extension eligible. Despite the 23-year-old forward needing offseason shoulder surgery, Hornets general manager Jeff Peterson said Miller should be a full participant in training camp.

Is there enough spacing on this roster to allow Caleb Wilson and Matas Buzelis to develop offensively? Jalen Smith and Norman Powell were the only players on the roster to average at least 37% shooting from deep on a minimum of three attempts per game last season. The Bulls should get a boost with the addition of Buddy Hield. Acquired in a trade from Charlotte, Hield is a 39.5% career shooter from 3. During Tiago Splitter's season as the interim coach in Portland, the Trail Blazers finished third in 3-point attempts but 27th in 3-point percentage.

Does Cleveland have enough depth if Peyton Watson, Evan Mobley or Jarrett Allen miss time? Allen and Watson combined to play 110 games with Denver last season. During the Cavaliers' postseason, frontcourt reserves Thomas Bryant (appeared in nine of 18 games) and Nae'Qwan Tomlin (appeared in seven) failed to reach five minutes per game. What to watch during training camp: return of Kyrie Irving and health of Dereck Lively II

Irving hasn't played since March 3, 2025, when he tore his left ACL in a home loss against the Sacramento Kings. A healthy Irving will improve an offense that ranked 22nd in assists and 29th in made 3s.

Lively has played 43 of 165 games over the past two seasons. Lively hasn't played since November due to a right foot injury that required surgery in December.

"[Lively] has been working his tail off. He's in the facility constantly, completely locked into everything we're doing and doing everything in his power to be his best self," Mavericks general manager Mike Schmitz told Dallas Hoops Journal in August. However, as ESPN's Tim MacMahon reported, Lively has not been cleared for training camp and his status for the season opener is uncertain.

What to watch during training camp: bench depth

The Nuggets return the same starting five that captured the Western Conference's No. 3 seed, including three-time MVP Nikola Jokic and first-time All-Star Jamal Murray. Denver's questions start with its depth. The Nuggets re-signed Spencer Jones and added veteran DeMar DeRozan but lost Tim Hardaway Jr., Bruce Brown, Peyton Watson and Jonas Valanciunas.

Hardaway ranked fifth on the Nuggets in points per game, while Watson ranked fifth in minutes per game. Jones is the only Denver reserve to average at least 20 minutes per game on a team that won at least half of its games since 2022-23.

Detroit Pistons

Contract snapshot

Guaranteed contracts: 12
Partial/non-guaranteed: 2

What to watch during training camp: Jalen Duren's restricted free agency. Duren remains unsigned despite coming off a season in which he averaged a career-high 19.5 points per game and became the first player since Charles Barkley in 1988-89 to record four games with 30 points, 10 rebounds on 80% shooting during the regular season.

If an agreement is not reached prior to Thursday, Duren could sign the $9.6 million one-year qualifying offer and enter unrestricted free agency in 2027. No player selected to an All-NBA or All-Star team has ever signed the qualifying offer. If Duren -- who was named All-NBA and selected as an All-Star last season -- becomes a free agent next summer, eight teams project to have enough cap space to sign him.

Golden State Warriors

Contract snapshot

Guaranteed contracts: 12
Partial/non-guaranteed: 4

What to watch during training camp: extensions, injury returns and frontcourt depth

Extension talks between the Warriors and Brandin Podziemski are a headline entering training camp. The 23-year-old guard is rookie-extension-eligible until Oct. 19. After Golden State extended Stephen Curry, it projects to have between $38 million and $55 million in cap space next summer. If Podziemski extends for more than $17 million -- the amount of his free agent hold -- Golden State loses financial flexibility.

Elsewhere on the roster, expect an updated injury timeline soon on Jimmy Butler III and Moses Moody; Butler tore his right ACL in January, while Moody ruptured his left patellar tendon in late March. Golden State was a plus-7.6 per 100 possessions when both players were on the court last season.

The Warriors extended Kristaps Porzingis and re-signed Al Horford. Even with both players returning, there are questions about the lack of frontcourt depth. And the health of Porzingis and Horford also is an area of concern, as the big man duo combined to miss nearly half of their games with the Warriors last season. (Porzingis is out indefinitely with a health issue.)

Unless coach Steve Kerr elects to go small with Draymond Green at the 5, Charles Bassey is the only other big on the roster. Bassey, a 25-year-old center, has yet to average more than 15.5 minutes per game, as he appeared in just 13 games last season between the Warriors, Celtics, 76ers and Grizzlies.

Date to watch

Oct. 19: deadline to extend the contracts of Podziemski and Moody

Extension candidates and eligibility

Moody (three years, $67.1 million; Oct. 1-19)
Podziemski (rookie extension; through Oct. 19)

Houston Rockets

Contract snapshot

Guaranteed contracts: 12
Partial/non-guaranteed: 2
Exhibit 10: 2
Two-way: 3

What to watch during training camp: playmaking

Fred VanVleet's season-ending knee injury that he suffered before 2025 training camp played a major role in the Rockets' offensive regression. With VanVleet on the court in 2024-25, Houston ranked 12th in offense and was 26-18 in clutch games. With the veteran guard recovering from a torn right ACL, the Rockets ranked 20th in offense and were 18-19 in clutch games. After electing to not sign a fill-in facilitator, Houston ranked 24th in both assist-to-turnover ratio and in turnovers committed. VanVleet's return and the free agent signings of Marcus Smart and Bogdan Bogdanovic should help the Rockets' offense operate more smoothly.

Dates to watch

Nov. 2: deadline to exercise the team option of Reed Sheppard

Extension candidates and eligibility: None

Indiana Pacers

Contract snapshot

Guaranteed contracts: 14
Partial/non-guaranteed: 0
Exhibit 10: 2
Two-way: 3

What to watch during training camp: Tyrese Haliburton and Ivica Zubac

It is rare for a team that won 19 games the prior season to be considered a conference favorite. Indiana is different for multiple reasons.

The Pacers return 10 players, including All-Stars Haliburton and Pascal Siakam, from the roster that pushed Oklahoma City to seven games in the 2025 NBA Finals. Haliburton tore his right Achilles in Game 7 of that series and missed the entire 2025-26 campaign.

When Haliburton last played, the Pacers were plus-4.1 points per 100 possessions in the regular season and plus-7.8 in the postseason with their floor general on the court. He had 33 games with at least 10 assists and boasted a 5.6 assist-to-turnover ratio in 2024-25.

A healthy Haliburton will be tasked with reviving an offense that ranked 27th overall, 26th in field goal percentage, 20th in 3-point shooting and 18th in fast-break points -- while working alongside a non-shooting big man in Zubac.

stories.headline: Ayrton Senna's Honda NSX could fetch £800,000 at London auction
stories.summary: A 1991 Honda NSX that once belonged to Ayrton Senna will go up for auction in London at the end of October.
stories.body:
A 1991 Honda NSX that once belonged to Ayrton Senna will go up for auction in London at the end of October.

Chassis number T000233 was one of three NSXs delivered to Senna as part of his contract with Honda in the early 1990s and, due to its provenance, carries an estimate of £500,000 to £800,000.

When the car first went on sale in 1990 it had a list price of between £52,000 and £55,000, with low-mileage NSXs from the same era currently listed online for up to £135,000.

The legendary Japanese sports car is closely linked to Senna, who contributed to its development before it went on sale as Honda's answer to the more expensive Porsche and Ferrari sportscars of the era.

Chassis T000233 is finished in Formula Red over a black leather interior and was delivered to Portugal in March 1991 so that Senna could make use of it while staying at his property in Quinta do Lago.

According to the listing on Sotheby's website, the NSX featured in the 1992 documentary, 'Ayrton Senna: Racing Is In My Blood' and was used by the Brazilian to commute to the 1991 Portuguese Grand Prix in Estoril.

Senna, who died in an accident at the 1994 San Marino Grand Prix, won all three of his world titles with Honda power while racing at McLaren.

stories.headline: Former draftee slams AFL over concussion plight
stories.summary: An AFL draftee whose life was upended by a concussion injury says he "was so close to ending everything".
stories.body:
An AFL draftee whose life was upended by a concussion injury says he "was so close to ending everything".

Aiden O'Driscoll, who had to retire because of a devastating training injury without making his AFL debut, also slammed the league as an "absolute joke".

"The last couple of years I've experienced nothing but pain, and I've explained it multiple times to you. You're supposed to help AFL players through hardship, not leave them with absolutely nothing," O'Driscoll wrote in his extensive Instagram post.

His comments came a day after Geelong announced defender Jake Kolodjashnij had retired.

Last month, the Cats were fined $140,000 and current AFL chairman Craig Drummond apologised after it emerged the club had agreed to a secret concussion waiver with Kolodjashnij. Drummond was Geelong president at the time the agreement was struck.

The Geelong controversy highlighted the complexity and sensitivity around contact sport's concussion crisis.

The Western Bulldogs recruited O'Driscoll in the 2023 draft. But a head injury that summer left him with significant ongoing health problems and the club announced in May, 2024 that he had retired on medical grounds.

"The doctors described my concussion as 'one of the worst' they've seen, with eight micro brain bleeds, and (a) fracture behind my ear," O'Driscoll wrote.

"From a medical point of view, losing my career, my identity plus going through the symptoms I have, you'd think the AFL would be useful with some support?

O'Driscoll added it took the AFL six weeks to find him a psychologist.

"Through this period, I was grieving the most, it got to the point where I started questioning my life? If it was worth living?," he wrote.

"I was so close to ending everything, I would've been free from all the pain/trauma. My family/close friends and partners honestly kept me here."

Melbourne premiership player Angus Brayshaw also had to retire in 2024 because of his concussion issues.

In his emotional toast to other retiring players at the Brownlow Medal function that year, Brayshaw referred to O'Driscoll by name.

"I know a few other past players that are dealing with the same issues as I am," O'Driscoll said.

"AFL it's time to step up! I'm a 21-year-old that can't keep suffering each week. While you're at it, help the other past players that need support."

O'Driscoll added he had been told at 18 never to play contact sport again.

The AFL and the players' association were contacted for comment.

stories.summary: Here's a look at every weight class to determine the best of the best in UFC, PFL and beyond.
stories.body:
Bad blood between UFC women's bantamweight title contenders Norma Dumont and Ailin Perez boiled over during their faceoff a day ahead of Saturday's fight, with matchmaker Sean Shelby forced to keep the fighters separated from each other.

The next night, when the fight concluded with Perez announced as the winner, Dumont appeared shocked by the unanimous decision and Perez turned her back on Dumont and twerked in her direction. The fighters had to be separated again before being escorted from the cage.

The fight that happened in between those fiery moments? It was not nearly as fierce. It began with a Round 1 in which Dumont landed eight significant strikes and Perez only four. And while the action picked up a little in the two rounds that followed, the women mostly circled each other.

But Perez got the win, and as a result, she moved up two spots to No. 2 in the ESPN women's bantamweight rankings, bumping Dumont down to No. 3.

That is the only movement in the latest rankings.

stories.summary: Nathan Cleary has completed rugby league's boxed set, with the Penrith star claiming his maiden Dally M Medal after romping to a dominant victory at the NRL's gala night.
stories.body:
Nathan Cleary's rugby league box set is complete, with the Penrith star claiming his maiden Dally M Medal after romping to a dominant victory at the NRL's gala night.

Unable to attend after his horror ankle injury in Penrith's preliminary final loss, Cleary accepted Wednesday night's award from his couch.

The Panthers champion finished 14 points clear of Cronulla half Braydon Trindall, who was in the hunt until a dislocated shoulder ended his regular season.

Tamika Upton also claimed her third Dally M Medal as NRLW player of the year, defending her crown from last year when the Brisbane fullback became the award's first multiple winner.

Warriors mentor Andrew Webster pipped Justin Holbrook to be the NRL's coach of the year with finals not counted, while Canberra playmaker Ethan Sanders was rookie of the year.

But the story of the night was Cleary, who left hospital on Wednesday after undergoing emergency surgery on his ankle.

Despite being the best player of this decade, the Dally M had somehow evaded Cleary due to a run of injuries or suspensions.

But he played 23 games this year, setting up 29 tries and acting as the chief architect of Penrith's run to a preliminary final.

Cleary led the race for the majority of the year, polling 67 votes ahead of Trindall's 53 and Panther Dylan Edwards' 52.

"I can't thank everyone enough for the messages they've sent through and the support I've felt," Cleary said.

"In terms of being able to win the Dally M award, I'm super grateful for that as well.

"I want to start off by thanking all my teammates. None of this would be possible without them. They definitely made me 10,000 times the player that I am."

Cleary had earlier this year claimed his maiden Wally Lewis Medal, silencing his critics by leading NSW to a 2-1 State of Origin series victory.

The 28-year-old has also won two Clive Churchill Medals to go with his four premierships at Penrith.

Meanwhile, Newcastle's magical run to the grand final was not reflected in the Dally M team of the year, with the Knights having no players in the side.

Kalyn Ponga also missed out on captain of the year and Holbrook as coach, with all voting complete at the end of the regular season, when the Knights finished seventh.

Robert Toia and Naufahu Whyte were the two Sydney Roosters representatives named in the side.

In the NRLW, Upton's win came after she polled six points in the penultimate round and then one point in Round 11 to beat Wests Tigers' half Raecene McGregor.

The Broncos No.1 is now the clear best player in the women's game over the opening eight years of the NRLW.

"I've still got lots to improve on," Upton said, with Sunday's grand final against Sydney Roosters still looming.

"We've seen that this year. I have been learning being a sole captain this year.

"We went through a tricky patch this year and I learnt a lot about myself as an individual, but a footy player as well."

Newcastle winger Mercedez Taulelei-Siala was named rookie of the year, after a season when she scored 13 tries in 12 games. Gold Coast mentor Karyn Murphy won the coach's medal.

The heart-touching moment of the night came when South Sydney's Jai Arrow was presented the Peter Frilingos headline moment and the Provan-Summons spirit of the game award for the way he has approached his battle with motor neurone disease.

NRL TEAM OF THE YEAR:

Dylan Edwards, Thomas Jenkins, Herbie Farnworth, Robert Toia, Selwyn Cobbo, Braydon Trindall, Nathan Cleary, James Fisher-Harris, Wayde Egan, Naufahu Whyte, Haumole Olakau'atu, Hamish Stewart, Erin Clark. Coach: Andrew Webster.

NRLW TEAM OF THE YEAR

Tamika Upton, Julia Robinson, Isabelle Kelly, Jess Sergis, Brydie Parker, Teagan Levi, Raecene McGregor, Millie Elliott, Keeley Nizza, Sarah Togatuki, Evania Isa'ako, Shaylee Bent, Olivia Kernick. Coach: Karyn Murphy.

stories.headline: Independent Football Regulator chief: Man City guilty verdict 'raises serious issues'
stories.summary: Manchester City's guilty verdict for breaching Premier League financial rules "raises serious issues", according to the chair of English football's independent regulator.
stories.body:
Manchester City's guilty verdict for breaching Premier League financial rules "raises serious issues," according to the chair of English football's independent regulator.

An independent commission has concluded City "clearly intended to circumvent Premier League rules" by inflating revenue and hiding costs over a nine-season period.

David Kogan, the chair of the Independent Football Regulator (IFR), pointed out his body has the power to assess the suitability of club owners and executives "where appropriate," when there is "clear evidence of wrongdoing by individuals."

City have already indicated their intention to appeal, describing the decision as "unsafe," and drew support from former manager Pep Guardiola in an X post on Wednesday afternoon.

Kogan acknowledged the City case remains ongoing but outlined the powers the IFR could bring into play should the appeal board broadly uphold the decision of the original commission.

"The independent commission's decision raises serious issues," Kogan said.

"The IFR has powers to assess the suitability of owners, directors and executives and we will use these powers where appropriate, in the interests of protecting the sustainability, honesty and integrity of English football where there is clear evidence of wrongdoing by individuals.

"This includes taking account of findings made by the leagues. However, as the proceedings remain ongoing between Manchester City and the Premier League we will await further developments.

"We hope it can be resolved quickly for the sake of fans. For now, we have no further comment."

In the most extreme cases, the IFR has statutory powers to force directors and managers off boards and to compel owners to divest from clubs.

Guardiola, who won six Premier League titles with City before leaving at the end of last season, issued a social media post via the Pep Team X account in solidarity with the club's bosses, players, coach and supporters.

"I want every single Man City fan to know I am here; more than ever. I am, always have been, always will, be behind my club, my owner, my chairman, Ferran, the players, staff, Enzo and you, our unique supporters," the post read.

"Let me be clear: we will get through this together. I love you all."

City were found to have engaged in schemes to inflate revenue and hide costs to the tune of more than £900 million ($1.2b billion) to avoid breaching Premier League and UEFA rules.

The club have already indicated their intention to appeal, and have said the decision "contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe."

City chief executive Ferran Soriano told staff in a video message that the commission had gone along with the Premier League's "conspiracy theory."

- Pep Guardiola after Man City guilty verdict: 'I am behind my club'

- Man City to appeal guilty verdict in Premier League breaches case

- Roy Keane: I'd put Man City medals 'in the bin' after 'cheating'

The Times, meanwhile, has reported that other top-flight clubs have contacted the league urging a conclusion to the case before the end of the season.

The same commission which has given its decision will now consider what sanctions should be imposed.

These could include significant sporting punishments, such as a points deduction, or even expulsion.

That would be a dramatic fall from grace for a club who have won eight Premier League titles since Sheikh Mansour's 2008 takeover.

The club were found by the commission to have operated a "disguised funding scheme" whereby companies from Abu Dhabi paid a fraction of the sum recorded on the club's books, with the balance settled by Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG), the company through which Sheikh Mansour owns the club.

That scheme was found to have inflated revenue by more than £830m ($1.1 billion) over the nine-season period between 2009-10 and 2017-18.

The club also were found to have overstated income from image rights by almost £74m ($98.2m), and understated liabilities for staff contracts by almost £17m ($22.5m.)

City were also found to have made "concerted efforts" to "stop and frustrate" the Premier League's investigation.

stories.headline: A guide to NHL goalie masks for the 2026-27 season
stories.summary: Here's a look at the notable goalie mask designs across the NHL for the upcoming season.
stories.body:
The NHL season is finally here, and with it comes renewed optimism and high hopes for fans' favorite teams. It also brings fresh lids for goalies across the league.

Goaltenders continue to push the envelope when it comes to their masks. Some like to keep it simple, while others enjoy standing out. Unique colors, nods to the city they play in and favorite movies are all represented in designs.

Washington Capitals goalie Logan Thompson fits into the latter category, highlighting two films with D.C. ties. Philadelphia Flyers goaltender Joseph Woll shows off his love for the "Lord of the Rings" series on one lid, while also repping the City of Brotherly Love on another. And of course, it wouldn't be a list of mask designs without Edmonton Oilers' Tristan Jarry repping his dogs.

Here's a look at some of the notable goalie masks this season.

Anaheim Ducks

Lukas Dostal

Dostal first unveiled this mask in April, and it looks to have carried over to the new season. It's a simple design with Ducks logos scattered throughout.

Boston Bruins

Jeremy Swayman

There is no shortage of Boston-specific elements to Swayman's mask, which follows a historical theme. It includes landmarks such as the USS Constitution and Boston Custom House Tower. And of course, there's a bruin above the face mask.

Buffalo Sabres

Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen

Nicknamed "Buffalo Rage," Luukkonen brings back this look from last year and it features an animal breaking out from ice for a menacing design.

Alex Lyon

Lyon's mask also carries over from last season and includes a buffalo on both sides, with a drawing of legendary Sabres goalie Dominik Hasek also featured.

Calgary Flames

Dustin Wolf

The elements of Wolf's mask are hard to ignore: a huge wolf and flames, plus a cowboy on the side for a neat design.

Carolina Hurricanes

Brandon Bussi

Bussi first debuted this look during Carolina's Stanley Cup run last season. It returns with the Canes logo on the side and puzzle pieces on the top, shining a light on autism awareness.

Pyotr Kochetkov

Kochetkov has worn this mask for a couple of seasons, and it won't be hung up in the locker room for good anytime soon. The raging bear on top is back for another campaign.

Chicago Blackhawks

Spencer Knight

Paying homage to the 100-year anniversary of the Blackhawks, Knight rocked this mask last season.

Colorado Avalanche

Scott Wedgewood

Wedgewood has a neatly painted design with two unlikely figures featured: Daphne Blake from "Scooby-Doo" and Scarlet Witch from Marvel.

Mackenzie Blackwood

The Colorado references are strong with Blackwood's clean and crisp design.

Columbus Blue Jackets

Jet Greaves

Greaves has a simple lid with the Blue Jackets' cannon included on the right and left side of the look.

Dallas Stars

Jake Oettinger

Oettinger has his options this season and they follow the same theme: monster otters. There's a light and dark green version, with each of them equally menacing.

Detroit Red Wings

John Gibson

White tentacles slither around Gibson's lid for a sleek and chic design.

Edmonton Oilers

Tristan Jarry

A dog is a man's best friend, and in this case, a dog is a goalie's best friend. Jarry has his dogs prominently featured on his mask with Tom and Jerry from the iconic cartoon show also painted on the top.

Florida Panthers

Jacob Markstrom

Playing for the Panthers, it's no surprise Markstrom has the animal on the top with glowing red eyes and an open mouth under the face mask. There are other subtle details, too, like the Fort Lauderdale skyline.

Akira Schmid

Similar to Markstrom, the Fort Lauderdale skyline is featured on Schmid's mask, as well as a panther on top.

Los Angeles Kings

Darcy Kuemper

The beach isn't too far from the Kings' home in downtown Los Angeles, therefore, Kuemper's look includes references to the city's famous beaches.

Anton Forsberg

Los Angeles is also known as the "City of Angels." Forsberg leans into the angel theme with sculptures painted on both sides. His two children are also included on the back with angel wings next to them.

Minnesota Wild

Jesper Wallstedt

Wallstedt's mask is all about bringing the wild to life with pine trees popping out.

Montreal Canadiens

Sam Montembeault

Montembeault first unveiled this python-themed look last season, and it's back for another campaign.

Jakub Dobes

Dobes' lid follows a "Game of Thrones" theme with a giant wolf on top that has glowing swords sticking up under it.

Nashville Predators

Juuse Saros

Saros' yellow lid is a continuation of his previous styles with predators on the side and a menacing skull on top.

New Jersey Devils

Jake Allen

Allen has three simple looks to choose from, each of them with similar designs: a devils logo on top being the main carryover.

Nico Daws

The Devils' colors are prominent on Daws' lid for a simple, yet effective look.

New York Islanders

Ilya Sorokin

Playing to the theme of the Islanders, the retro design includes a ghost pirate captain on one side and a larger ship on the other for a neat lid.

New York Rangers

Igor Shesterkin

It's no surprise that playing in New York prompted a big apple being painted on Shesterkin's mask. However, it also includes multiple New York City-specific details, such as the city skyline and Brooklyn Bridge.

Joonas Korpisalo

Korpisalo is throwing it back to the 1970s and '80s for a classic feel that also includes New York City-specific details.

Ottawa Senators

Linus Ullmark

If you had a mask design inspired by Norse mythology on your bingo card, it's your lucky day. Ullmark's lid focuses on the battle between the giant wolf Fenrir and the Norse god Tyr. Both are featured prominently for a menacing look while the Senators logo is on the other side.

Philadelphia Flyers

Joseph Woll

Woll might have the best mask rotation in the league this season.

One of them is a tribute to "The Lord of the Rings" series, of which Woll is a big fan. It's about the battle between Gandalf and Balrog, which included the famous line: "You shall not pass!" The other pays homage to Philadelphia and prominently features Benjamin Franklin flying a kite, the Liberty Bell and U.S. Constitution, among other items.

Dan Vladar

Vladar made headlines last season with a Metallica/Iron Maiden-themed mash up lid, and it returns once again.

Pittsburgh Penguins

Sergei Murashov

Hailing from Russia, Murashov wanted a lid that incorporated elements of his home and Pittsburgh. The outcome is one that focuses on Russia in one half, and Pittsburgh on the other.

Arturs Silovs

No different than Murashov, Silovs pays homage to his home country of Latvia. Most notably, his design includes details from the Latvian hockey team emblem on the chin.

San Jose Sharks

Yaroslav Askarov

Askarov's mask includes many different shades of blue with a menacing shark on top.

Alex Nedeljkovic

Sharks are all over Nedeljkovic's lid, but "Ned" on the chin might be the detail that stands out the most.

Seattle Kraken

Joey Daccord

Daccord is a huge fan of Formula 1, therefore, it's no surprise that his new mask focuses on that love with a custom F1 car painted on alongside other Seattle-specific elements. There's a darker lid he can choose from, too, appropriate for the Kraken's all-black uniforms.

Philipp Grubauer

Designed by local Seattle glass artist Preston Singletary, Grubauer first debuted this mask in 2024 for the Kraken's Indigenous Peoples Night. The two-sided design remains in Grubauer's mix as he wore it during the preseason.

St. Louis Blues

Jordan Binnington

It's a retro look for Binnington with drawings on the side that are close to home for the goaltender.

Joel Hofer

Hofer also leans into a classic design, a simple white one with musical notes throughout it.

Tampa Bay Lightning

Andrei Vasilevskiy

"Gzhel," a style of blue and white ceramics inspired by a village near Moscow, is often the theme of Vasilevskiy's lids and it continues this season with a sweet look.

Toronto Maple Leafs

Sergei Bobrovsky

Bobrovsky's lid might not have too many elements, but that doesn't mean it won't stand out. It's built on a brick wall background with the Archangel Michael prominently drawn on one side, while the Maple Leafs logo is on the other.

Anthony Stolarz

Chrome is the name of the game for Stolarz's mask, which was created in chrome FX, a special coat for a unique look.

Utah Mammoth

Karel Vejmelka

A huge mammoth is the star of Vejmelka's design, but there are other elements of Utah included, like the Delicate Arch.

Vancouver Canucks

Kevin Lankinen

Lankinen has a simple design full of nods to Vancouver, including the city's skyline and mountains.

Vegas Golden Knights

Adin Hill

A menacing dragon covers Hill's mask for an eye-popping gold-and-red look.

Carter Hart

Inspired by the 1993 Western film "Tombstone," Hart unveiled this lid before the 2026 Stanley Cup playoffs.

Washington Capitals

Logan Thompson

Thompson is known for his movie-themed masks and this season is no different. One pays homage to the 1996 film "Mars Attacks!" while the other is about the 2005 hit movie "Wedding Crashers." Both movies include ties to Washington, D.C., making this one that hits close to home, too.

Winnipeg Jets

Stuart Skinner

Skinner has two contrasting colored designs to pick from, but they are equally sleek. The all-white mask boasts a polar bear with a hockey stick and the Provencher Bridge. The darker blue one follows an aviation theme for a look that pops.

stories.headline: Fantasy basketball: The pros and cons of points, roto and category leagues
stories.summary: Which fantasy basketball scoring format should you play? Jim McCormick breaks down the most popular options so you can choose for yourself.
stories.body:
They often say in boxing that styles make fights. The idiom suggests that unique approaches and strategies to the same sport can prove compelling. A southpaw slugger against a quick-footed righty adds to the sweetness of the science.

In a fantasy sports context, formats make things more fun.

When it comes to fantasy basketball, some managers are drawn to a season-long balancing act; curating each statistical category to remain competitive in 3-pointers while also making sure to have enough rim protection. Such managers would be ideal for rotisserie (roto) leagues -- or weekly head-to-head category leagues -- where statistical balance across your roster is the ultimate goal.

Others might prefer to compete in something closer to the fantasy football experience; which we call points leagues in fantasy hoops. These leagues lean on a scoring legend that rewards a specific number of points for each stat accumulated (one point for a rebound, four points for a block, for instance). Check out ESPN's default scoring for points leagues to better understand how this format values each category.

With this in mind, we've done some of the work for you; laying out the pros and cons of roto/category and points-driven formats to help refine the process. The good news is that you can also choose to play in each of these unique formats if you participate in multiple leagues.

How do Roto and H2H Category leagues work?
Roto leagues

Using a 10-team roto league as an example, the team that has the most steals by the end of the season earns 10 points, while the least-larcenous team is left with a single point. This is true for each of the categories your league employs.

Each starting roster spot is afforded an 82-game limit, so maximizing games played isn't an applicable angle in the vein that it fuels success in weekly head-to-head competition. That said, you don't want to fall behind too far in games logged, either, as your competition might end up many games ahead once spring arrives.

As for the specific categories your roto or categories league selects, it's advisable to go with a traditional eight-category setup (points, rebounds, steals, blocks, assists, 3-pointers and both field goal and free throw percentages) versus including turnovers, which are ultimately a tax on ball-dominant players. Some possible additions for a ninth category: assist-to-turnover ratio, which considers turnovers but also values efficient distribution and ball-security, or double-doubles, which put more emphasis on bigs who can rebound.

In roto, the team with the highest total of cumulative points in across each category takes home the title. There are no playoffs or late-season upsets to consider, as we must in weekly head-to-head leagues. This does not mean the format isn't exciting or compelling; roto merely demands a season-long grind from managers. Finally catching your friend in steals thanks to an awesome surge of swipes from Marcus Smart in early April is undeniably rewarding.

H2H Category leagues

Another fun format, head-to-head category leagues, stems from the old-school energy of rotisserie, but is a bit more modernized in that teams compete each week. My home league, for instance, competes head-to-head weekly just like a fantasy football format might, but we use the nine categories noted in the prior paragraph. So, for instance, a dominant week might see you go 7-2 across said categories, while many weeks the margins are 5-4 or 6-3. The top records head to the playoffs come spring.

In these two formats, we covet players who can contribute a consistently diverse collection of statistics, as each category is weighted equally in regards to points. Which is to say, you don't get more points for leading your roto league in points than you do for pacing the competition in steals -- it simply all matters in this format.

The Pros of Roto and Category Leagues

Nuance and balance drive success. Basketball is a sport that counts so many meaningful statistics, while football is largely centered around touchdowns, receptions, and yardage.
Research with a purpose is rewarded. It takes an ability to recognize which 3-point specialist can also find you steals (i.e., Gary Trent Jr.), or which shot-blockers won't tank your free-throw accuracy (i.e., Brook Lopez or Jaren Jackson Jr.).
In rotisserie leagues, the full season plays out. The volatility of a playoff bracket is removed. The winner is truly the most balanced and well-crafted team. There is some volatility present in head-to-head category leagues, but the balance of leveraging eight-to-nine categories also buffers the upset factors that we find in points leagues.

The Cons of Roto and Category Leagues

It's a grind. In what is a counter to some of the pros above, not all of us want to carefully balance our fantasy rosters. Sometimes, it's just fun to chase volume over nuance.
It's tougher to make a comeback: In a roto league, as the games mount, it becomes more daunting to scale the standings if you've punted (ignored a category) or simple fell victim to lots of injuries. This makes staying enthused into the spring more challenging for some.

How do Points leagues work?
The total points generated by the players on your roster are tallied each week, and you get a win or a loss that week based on whether you outscore your weekly opponent. If this sounds a lot like how weekly fantasy football works, it's because the formats are quite similar. At the end of the regular season, the top grouping of teams makes the playoffs and the final team left through this elimination bracket is champion.

The comparison to football isn't perfect, however, as the NBA season is obviously far longer and there are dozens more games played by each team. In most weeks, your fantasy basketball players will play three or four games rather than the singular outcomes of the NFL.

An extra two months of games helps remove some of the volatility and variance that can make fantasy football feel a bit vexing at times. With the marathon of the NBA, surviving a slow start is much more reasonable (shout out to those 1-4 fantasy football teams still keeping the dream alive). Even more fun is that basketball players have more on-and-off court time to develop over the course of the long season, unlike the sprint and unforgiving nature of the gridiron.

The joy of points leagues is the sheer value volume. Big-time scorers, rebounders, and playmakers drive some amazing point totals. Just imagine how many points a hot-streak from Nikola Jokic or Giannis Antetokounmpo might generate. Consider the elation of having helio-centric playmakers like Luka Doncic or Shai Gilgeous-Alexander driving your team to glory each week.

The Pros of Points Leagues

Volume is fun: Superstars shine brighter in the NBA more than maybe any other pro league. The single-named superstars: Luka, Embiid, "Joker," LeBron, et cetera, are even more celebrated when accumulation is king.
Aligns with our love for fantasy football. Week-by-week, it's about who has more points. The victor simply has more points.
Helps simplify a long season. Some want to have a fun and competitive companion to help augment the NBA marathon. While roto and category leagues are awesome for us spreadsheet warriors, points leagues are more accessible and relatable.

The Cons of Points Leagues

Lack of nuance. Basketball is an analytically-friendly game and points formats can in some ways oversimplify outcomes.
Volatility and variance: Many of us have had elite, once-in-a-decade fantasy basketball or football rosters felled by a single bad week in the fantasy playoffs. Such results are still natural in head-to-head points league in hoops.

What's right for you?
Recognizing that we have choices is empowering. Part of this power comes from being able to research and realize which type of fantasy league is best for us and our friends that we compete with throughout the NBA season.

stories.headline: Why is the Bahrain Grand Prix taking place in Malaysia, 4,000 miles away? F1's unusual race explained
stories.summary: Formula 1's next race has an odd quirk -- it is unofficially the rescheduled Bahrain Grand Prix, but it is taking place at Malaysia's Sepang International Circuit in Kuala Lumpur.
stories.body:
Formula 1's next race has an odd quirk. Look at the calendar and you'll see the rescheduled Bahrain Grand Prix. The only catch? It is taking place at Malaysia's Sepang International Circuit in Kuala Lumpur.

You don't have to be a geography buff to know those two places are not the same, nor are they close on the map. The bizarre event all comes down to global politics and is part of a wider situation that has left the destination of F1's season-ending races -- events in Qatar and Abu Dhabi -- uncertain, too.

Here's everything you need to know about F1's first "Middle Eastern" race of the year, and the current status of the final two races in the region which are meant to close the 2026 season.

- Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia 2026: Race start time, how to watch, full schedule, predictions

- Russell's win won't kick-start title challenge, but Baku rewards his faith in trying 2026

First things first, what are we calling this race?
Amusingly, perhaps slightly farcically, F1's next race will be called the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, held on Oct. 4, sandwiched between events in Baku and Singapore. It means another triple header on the calendar, with the season already due (as it stands) to feature Austin-Mexico City-Brazil, a gap, then Las Vegas-Qatar-Abu Dhabi.

While a slightly ridiculous naming convention, the event does mark a welcome and surprise return for the hugely popular Sepang circuit, which last hosted a race in 2017 after 18 years on the calendar. F1 understands the official flag next to the event will be Bahrain's, and the winner of the race will be considered to be a winner of the Bahrain Grand Prix in F1's official record books.

What national anthem will play before the event?
Exact plans remain to be seen, though sources have told ESPN that pre-race grid plans feature both the Bahrain and Malaysian flags, while Bahrain's national band is also in Malaysia for the event.

What happened to Bahrain's original race?
The decision not to hold races in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia in April was a by-product of ongoing hostilities in the Middle East, triggered by a wave of attacks launched on Iran by the United States and Israel in March. That saw a number of countries in the region struck by Iran in response -- including Bahrain and Saudi Arabia. Bahrain's capital Manama was hit just weeks after it had hosted preseason testing.
As a result, F1 cancelled what would have been back-to-back races, the Bahrain Grand Prix on April 12 and Jeddah's Saudi Arabian Grand Prix on April 19. That left a four-week gap in the calendar between the Japanese Grand Prix and the Miami Grand Prix without a race. Importantly, at the time F1 made it clear the door was open for both events to happen later in the year should the situation in the region cool down.

Was rescheduling either event a realistic option?
Originally, F1 hoped it might be able to reschedule one or both events if and when the situation in the region cooled. Bahrain naturally was the easier option -- it's a permanent facility and, having hosted preseason and in anticipation of the event that should have taken place in April, some freight remains there which never left the nation state. That meant there was automatically a lot more flexibility around rearranging Bahrain if the opportunity had presented itself. As for Saudi Arabia, that was more complicated -- the Jeddah event is a street circuit around the city, for one thing, and street circuits naturally require a bit more lead-time in terms of preparation.

Sources have told ESPN that while Bahrain were happy to host an event wherever possible, Saudi's organisers had been set on rescheduling their race as a season-ending race. Even without a massive de-escalation in the Middle East, that presented big issues -- the season is already due to finish on Dec. 6 in Abu Dhabi. To avoid an unprecedented four straight races, a Saudi race would likely have needed to be held in the middle of December or nearer Christmas time, which has never happened before. Then there's Abu Dhabi's place as the season-ender -- the UAE venue has been the long-time finale event and pays a premium for the privilege. Sources have told ESPN Abu Dhabi was not thrilled at the idea of letting a regional rival take that from them. All of that is irrelevant now, anyway -- Abu Dhabi and Qatar's races both look set to be cancelled due to the same conflict (more on that below).

Why did Malaysia help Bahrain out?
It might seem like a strange link-up on the surface, but the two nations actually share a close diplomatic relationship stretching back to 1974. Bahrain's King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa and Malaysia King Sultan Ibrahim Iskandar reportedly have a strong personal rapport. Sources have told ESPN the plan was first discussed in a conversation between the pair and a plan quickly unfolded from there. Bahrain had a race to reschedule and Malaysia had a beloved circuit completely free to step in. Malaysia offered to split the cost with Bahrain and it was seen as a win-win -- a good way to mark strong diplomatic ties between the two nations, while Bahrain gets to say it retained its grand prix on the 2026 calendar and Sepang gets the feel-good rub of stepping in and helping Bahrain and Formula 1 out in an hour of need.

Why was Bahrain so keen to hold a race, even if not on its own circuit?
Bahrain has been invested in F1 for a long time now. It first hosted a race in 2004 and has become a mainstay on the calendar, often as the season-opener, as well as becoming a regular and reliable preseason test venue. The nation state is also deeply intertwined with the sport -- Bahrain's sovereign wealth fund, Mumtalakat Holding Company, is majority owner of the McLaren team and full owner of the wider McLaren Group.

The scale of its involvement in F1 is far deeper than is currently the case in Saudi. But it wasn't just Bahrain that felt a need to get something sorted. The rearrangement is big from a contractual perspective for Formula 1 as well. The sport's commercial agreement with its 11 teams and its global broadcasters says the season cannot drop below 22 races -- should that ever happen, the financial cost for the sport would be severe. Bahrain and Saudi had already both been cancelled -- with Qatar and Abu Dhabi both likely to be canned at the end of the season, the sport effectively needed to find two replacements in quick time. Malaysia and Bahrain doing a deal meant F1 only had to find one race to finish the season with, should those other two events be cancelled as expected. As we will come to, easier options in Europe existed to fill a one-race gap.

What was Sepang like, and why did it stop hosting F1 in the first place?
Sepang enjoyed 18 years as a Formula 1 host between 1999 and 2017 and quickly established itself as a popular venue, with drivers loving its fast, flowing corners, while it boasts numerous places to overtake. Sepang actually was unlucky in the timing of its departure from the calendar -- Formula 1 was in a much less lucrative place at the time.

Liberty Media had only just taken over with a grand plan for the sport's growth, which has come to pass in the years since Covid. In 2017 things were not quite so rosy as they are now -- then-CEO of Sepang, Razlan Razali, told Reuters at the time: "It's hard to sell this kind of event and to get bums on the seats. It's not worth the investment at the moment." Of course, F1 has enjoyed stratospheric growth since the pandemic and most races are easy sellouts, with huge revenues and 11 teams all worth north of $1 billion (£753 million). Hindsight is 20-20, as they say.

Does this one-off return make Malaysia a candidate to host events again in the future?
It's hard to say for now. This event certainly can't hurt, and it's clear the event is in F1's good graces at the moment for stepping in. But it's not simply a case of it being fast-tracked to the front of the line for a future event. F1's calendar is already jam-packed at 24 events -- next year Portugal and Türkiye return, and F1 boss Stefano Domenicali often says there is a queue of potential venues waiting for a spot to open up, with the sport keen to prioritise an event in Africa in future if a viable venue materialises. Then there's Singapore, which may not be thrilled at the prospect of hosting a race so close to a neighbour every year. When Sepang was a regular host, Singapore and Malaysia were often next to each other on the calendar, but rarely just a week apart.
Isn't F1's season finishing in the Middle East as it stands? What about those two races?
As it stands, yes, although it seems likely that will change in the coming weeks after F1 bosses were told that they can expect a final decision by mid-October. The calendar as it stands says Qatar on Nov. 29 and Abu Dhabi on Dec. 6 will close the season, but F1 has been delaying a decision on both events as it monitors the situation in the region and there was hope the events could both go ahead as planned.

The World Endurance Championship, the series which holds the famous Le Mans 24 Hours, has already cancelled a race in Qatar that was due to be held in November. Sources have told ESPN that Italian circuit Imola will hold the season-ending race should Qatar and Abu Dhabi be cancelled. In that scenario, the race would take place on Dec. 6, the existing spot for Abu Dhabi's race. While eyebrows in the paddock have been raised at hosting a race in northern Italy in December, logistically the race presents an easy option, with all 11 teams based in Europe.

- Ferrari boss Fred Vasseur vents frustration over Christian Horner's F1 job search

- Charles Leclerc admits Ferrari's rivals have taken 'big steps forwards': 'We must not lie to ourselves'

Is Imola really the only option to step in?
Many in F1 have wondered the same thing, but the circuit has only just dropped off the calendar as a grand prix host, so its infrastructure is in place. Weather is far from ideal, with sunlight at a minimum and snow a regular feature, but the circuit has close ties to the sport which probably helped shuffle the historic venue to the front of the line -- it is the hometown of F1 CEO Domenicali and Ferrari's unofficial home race, given its close proximity to Ferrari's Maranello headquarters. Still, others wondered if other venues might be more appropriate.

F1 is due to race in Las Vegas the weekend before Thanksgiving, leaving many to speculate whether F1 could stay in America and race at Austin's Circuit of the Americas (COTA), which is already hosting a race on Oct. 24. However, COTA does not appear to have put itself forward nor does it appear to have been asked by F1 to stand in. Portugal's Portimao circuit was also floated as an option, but stepping in to host an event in December would have threatened the timeline of the renovations and upgrades the venue is doing in order to host a race next season. Imola, which dropped off the calendar after its 2025 race, has therefore emerged as the likely season-ender.

stories.headline: PSG chief Al-Khelaifi has 'zero interest' in FIFA presidency
stories.summary: European soccer's search for a candidate to challenge Gianni Infantino in the FIFA presidential election will not land on clubs' leader Nasser Al-Khelaifi.
stories.body:
GENEVA -- European soccer's search for a candidate to challenge Gianni Infantino in the FIFA presidential election will not land on clubs' leader Nasser Al-Khelaifi, the Paris Saint-Germain boss insisted Tuesday.

Al-Khelaifi also is chairman of the influential European Football Clubs group and so sits on the executive committee of UEFA, which is leading efforts to oust Infantino after his failed plan to sell stakes in future World Cup profits to private investors.

- Will anyone stop Infantino? FIFA president is confident U20 World Cup cameo says otherwise

- FIFA agrees in principle to federation payments from WC windfall

- FIFA accuses UEFA of 'misinformation campaign' over World Cup proposal

As a minister in the government of 2022 World Cup host Qatar -- which has so far supported Infantino -- Al-Khelaifi also could have broad appeal to FIFA voters in Asia, yet he moved to quash speculation he might try to lead soccer's governing body.

"I have zero interest in FIFA, zero agenda [or] ambition to be there," Al-Khelaifi said at a news conference after an EFC annual meeting in the Danish capital Copenhagen.

"I don't think I'm the right guy for this position and I don't want to go actually, I'm enjoying what I'm doing," the president of Champions League title holders PSG said. "I think FIFA's not for me. Thank you."

The annual meeting of the 900-member club was held amid a volatile time for soccer politics and Infantino's future.

It is two months after Infantino's multi-billion dollar FIFA subsidiary plan was revealed, then defeated within days, and seven weeks before the deadline for candidates to challenge him.

UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin is leading the campaign to end Infantino's presidency either before or at the March 18 election in Morocco, and he spoke to club leaders Tuesday.

"Football has no need for emperors," Ceferin said in a near 10-minute speech that did not name Infantino, whose biggest plans since his first election in 2016 have typically been seen as threats by his former employers at UEFA.

Ceferin's references, including creating an award for a politician, were clearly aimed at Infantino and his close working relations with U.S. President Donald Trump.

"It's time to say enough," said Ceferin, a FIFA vice president who has ruled himself out of being a candidate. "Rules bent when inconvenient. Those meant to have a say simply cut out. And football's future treated as just another bargaining chip."

Ceferin, like Infantino, was elected in 2016 -- in the fallout of FIFA's previous biggest crisis, provoked by U.S. and Swiss federal investigations -- and also can seek a fourth and final term in office next year.

"Football needs great leaders like you," Al-Khelaifi said of Ceferin in his own speech, adding "we ask you to stand for president again next year."

Ceferin, who said in 2024 he would leave office in 2027, is likely to be unopposed in the UEFA vote by 55 member federations scheduled in April in Astana, Kazakhstan.

stories.headline: Devils' rookies reveal reasons for inking deals
stories.summary: A chance to work under AFL development guru Nigel Lappin was a key carrot for the Tasmania Devils' first crop of signings.
stories.body:
A chance to work under AFL development guru Nigel Lappin was a key carrot for the Tasmania Devils' first crop of signings.

The club on Tuesday night unveiled their inaugural eight recruits, seven of them 17-year-olds who would have been eligible for the draft in 2027.

Top of the class was Western Australia's Axel Walsh, a forward ruck considered likely to be the No.1 pick at the next draft.

Walsh, who will move to Tasmania in November after finishing his schooling, said the opportunity to learn under head coach Ken Hinkley and Lappin was too good to refuse.

Three-time premiership winner Lappin was in August announced as the Devils' inaugural head of development, ending an 18-year association with Geelong.

The 50-year-old is regarded as one of the top developers in the league and previously turned down offers to stay with the Cats.

"Nigel at Geelong, we've seen the success they've had. I knew if the opportunity presented itself I would be silly to pass it up," Walsh said on Wednesday.

Despite being from the west, Walsh supported Geelong growing up and said he idolised Melbourne ruck star Max Gawn.

Walsh and his fellow rookies were presented with jumpers at a club event, where a video showing Tasmania's footy history and battles securing a licence was played.

"Tasmania's people have wanted a team for a very long time. It was goosebumps," Walsh said, denying he felt the weight of responsibility.

"Pressure is a privilege. All of us have worked hard to this point.

"We're just really excited to represent the island."

Small forward Angus Brown, who hails from the Sandringham Dragons, also said Lappin's presence was behind his decision to join the Devils.

And he said criticism that there isn't enough to do in Tasmania was off the mark.

"I'm not really thinking about it as a leap of faith," Brown said.

"There is a very nice vibe. Plenty of things to do, whether you're social or somebody who wants to get out in nature."

The Devils, who enter the AFL in 2028, will hope their rookies can follow a similar career trajectory to Jeremy Cameron, Adam Treloar and Dylan Shiel, who signed with GWS under the same list concession.

The eight could dip their toe into VFL footy in 2027, but will be developed on a case-by-case basis, Tasmania's head of list management and strategy Todd Patterson said.

stories.headline: Lone'er Kavanagh: Win in 'dangerous' UFC 333 fight puts me in title contention
stories.summary: Brit Lone'er Kavanagh believes victory against Ramazonbek Temirov at UFC 333 in Abu Dhabi could catapult him into flyweight title contention.
stories.body:
Brit Lone'er Kavanagh believes victory against Ramazonbek Temirov at UFC 333 in Abu Dhabi could catapult him into flyweight title contention.

Kavanagh (10-2) is coming off a fight of the night defeat to Brandon Royval in July, a result that followed his breakout win over former champion Brandon Moreno in Mexico City earlier this year.

Uzbekistan's Temirov (20-3) is yet to taste defeat in the UFC octagon and is on a 12-fight win streak.

Kavanagh has said that a positive result in the Middle East could reignite his momentum in the featherweight division after the submission defeat to Royval last time out.

"I believe so. I'd like to think [it puts me into the featherweight title mix]," Kavanagh told ESPN.

"I think a win there puts me right back up there. He's a dangerous opponent. He's got some good wins under him, a lot of wins, but I think a win against him puts me right back up at the top. [I'm] always looking for a finish.

"He's dangerous. He throws big shots, he throws wild shots. He's constantly [moving] forwards. He likes to stand and bang. Those are the main things I think that stick out. Obviously he's got a good wrestling background as well.

"His main weapons are his heavy hands, and that excites me. I love fights like that and I think it's a good fight for me.

"Hopefully [another fight of the night], I'm looking for more performances of the night. Kavanagh was unranked before his decision win against Moreno and will now be a part of his second numbered UFC card, with his last fight at the T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas on the night of Conor McGregor's ill-fated return against Max Holloway.

"It feels surreal, I'm very grateful I get these opportunities, being on a card with such big names, being high up, it's amazing. I'm very blessed," he said.

"If you told me 10 years ago I'd be fighting on cards like these, I'd have told you to do one, so it's very cool.

"It was an awesome opportunity to fight on that card, McGregor coming back, in Vegas, such a high-level fight. I'd like to think my style is entertaining as it is, I'm always looking to be in an entertaining fight and apart from that I just love fighting so just being in there is cool.

"I've gone from watching [UFC YouTube show] Embedded to actually being in it so that was cool!"

stories.headline: NRL Midweek Mail Grand Final: Halves injuries put Brooks on Penrith's radar
stories.summary: Daniel Tupou insists the result of the Grand Final will not decide whether he plays on, while Robert Toia is modest about his extraordinary talents.
stories.body:
The NRL rarely stands still.

Between training sessions, media appearances, and behind-the-scenes conversations, new storylines often begin to emerge before the weekend arrives.

Throughout the week, ESPN will be gathering notes, insights, and updates from around the competition heading into the NRL's Grand Final weekend.

Panthers emerge in Brooks race

Penrith have emerged as a potential destination for Luke Brooks should the veteran half depart Manly ahead of the 2027 season.

ESPN understands the Panthers are interested in Brooks, per multiple sources, as uncertainty continues around the playmaker's future at the Sea Eagles.

Brooks remains contracted to Manly through 2027, meaning any move for next season would require an early release, with Jamal Fogarty and highly rated youngster Joey Walsh the focus of the Sea Eagles' halves plans.

The Penrith link comes amid uncertainty surrounding their halves stocks for 2027.

Nathan Cleary and Blaize Talagi face lengthy injury recoveries, while Jack Cole will depart for the Perth Bears at season's end, leaving Jack Cogger as the Panthers' other established halves option.

Raiders eye Storm young gun

Canberra are keeping tabs on Melbourne Storm prop Josiah Pahulu ahead of the November 1 transfer window.

ESPN understands the Raiders are interested in the highly rated 22-year-old, who remains contracted to Melbourne through the end of 2027.

Pahulu joined the Storm from the Gold Coast midway through 2025 and has since continued his development in Melbourne's system.

Eligible to negotiate with rival clubs for 2028 from November 1, Pahulu has emerged as a player of interest for Canberra as clubs begin positioning themselves ahead of the market opening.

Amone commits to the Dragons

St George Illawarra have retained promising youngster Viliami Amone on a one-year deal for 2027 despite interest from several rival clubs, ESPN understands.

The younger brother of former Dragons playmaker Junior Amone was part of the club's Jersey Flegg side that claimed the 2026 minor premiership.

He played in the second row during the season and also earned four NSW Cup appearances as he progressed through the Dragons' pathways.

Tupou says Grand Final result won't decide his future

Daniel Tupou has put talks over his playing future on hold until after Sunday's Grand Final, but says the result will have no bearing on whether he continues next season.

Asked if winning a premiership might change his decision, the 35-year-old said:

"Not at all. I've just parked it for now in this finals series. Once this game's done, then I'll get back onto it."

Tupou said he still believes he has another year in him and confirmed family and friends have encouraged him to keep playing. For now, his focus is on a fourth Grand Final appearance with the Roosters.

Toia rejects top-three centre talk ahead of grand final

Robert Toia has played his way into conversations about the NRL's best centres, but the Roosters youngster believes a top-three ranking is premature.

"It's pretty good to hear, to be honest," Toia said of the praise.

"But I think that's exaggerated. I wouldn't say I'm a top-three centre.

"I feel like I've been playing somewhat good footy, but there's still a lot to show and still more to come."

Sunday's Grand Final offers a test against Bradman Best, whom Toia named among the most difficult centres to defend because of his size, speed and agility.

The pair have never met off the field, but Toia said he loves the matchup and is looking forward to measuring himself against the Newcastle star.

Familiar faces on the other side

Tupou said the Roosters are pleased to see former teammate Sandon Smith thriving at Newcastle, praising him as a player who delivered in big games during his time at the club. That goodwill will be set aside on Sunday.

Tupou is also preparing to face Dom Young, whose return to the Knights has set up a direct contest with his former Roosters teammate.

He said he did not know the details behind Young's exit and declined to speculate, but expects "a great battle" against the winger.
